- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:505-513 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: In `with_time` mode, the jq expression in `last_cycle_baseline_sha` is said to build a `{sha: null, at: $at}` object for a trusted comment that has no baseline marker. `last` would then select that comment and return `"null <created_at>"`.
  WHY: All three flaggers rated it MAJOR. The new caller `release_blocker_check_cycle_stale` (lines 1482-1492, sets `release_blocker_baseline_at` at line 1489) and the guard-4 caller (1618-1629, compare at 1630-1631) would consume an unrelated comment's timestamp or a `null` SHA, which could suppress `cycle_stale` reports or skip the baseline comparison. Disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash checked this claim and rejected it. They state that `capture(...)?` emits nothing on a non-match, so no object enters the array.
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py, tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: These test suites are said to fail as a direct result of this PR.
  WHY: The reviewer rated it BLOCKER and attributed the failures to the `id-token: write` permission added to the cycle job in .github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml, which "likely" trips guardrail or parity checks. Disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash state these tests read only files this PR does not touch, and that no failing assertion maps to a hunk in this diff.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:1467-1470 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The comment above `release_blocker_check_cycle_stale` still says "Reads no extra data.", but the function now calls `last_cycle_baseline_sha with_time` (lines 1482-1492). On pre-guard-4 skips such as `base_not_ancestor`, that call makes 1 search and up to 10 comment reads.
  WHY: All flaggers rated it NIT and confirmed there is no runtime effect. The comment misleads anyone auditing API cost under §14 or tracing the `lookup=baseline_marker` skip line.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:1092-1097 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The comment on `release_blocker_baseline_read` says it is "Set once guard 4's marker search succeeded", but `release_blocker_check_cycle_stale` now also sets it at line 1489 after its own fallback marker read.
  WHY: All flaggers rated it NIT. The comment no longer matches the code, and there is no runtime effect.
- README.md:288 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `RELEASE_BLOCKER_CYCLE_STALE_SECS` row documents the fallback marker read ("1 search plus up to 10 comment reads") but keeps "(no extra API call; nothing is reported when neither time is known)" in the same sentence, so the row contradicts itself.
  WHY: All flaggers rated it NIT. This row is the operator reference for the reporter's API cost, and it misstates the extra GETs on `base_not_ancestor` ticks. Fix suggested by anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5: drop "no extra API call;" or limit it to skips after guard 4.
- agents.d/stuck-states-p4-rb-cycle-reporters.md:2 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `cycle_stale` clause omits the pre-guard-4 marker self-read (1 search plus up to 10 comment reads) and its failure line `RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORT_SKIPPED ... lookup=baseline_marker`, while the README and the script header both document them.
  WHY: Both flaggers rated it NIT. The fragment has drifted from the README, and the text that folds into agents.md leaves out the reporter's cost and failure mode. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 raised the same point as a hardening suggestion, not as a finding.
- tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:after line 1720 (`test_diverged_stable_branch_still_reports_cycle_stale`, `test_diverged_stable_branch_with_recent_marker_does_not_report`, `_diverged_stale_state`) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Both new tests use `_stale_state(...)` with exactly one `cycle_comments` entry, the baseline-marker comment. No test mixes in a trusted comment without a marker posted after the real marker.
  WHY: The reviewer rated it MAJOR. The input shape that would trigger the jq `with_time` finding on the newly activated `base_not_ancestor` path is not covered by any test.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:lines 505-513 (the jq expression inside `last_cycle_baseline_sha` with `with_time` mode, consumed by the new caller at lines 1482-1492) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The jq pipeline keeps every trusted comment even when `capture(...)` finds no marker. `last` picks the most recent trusted comment and emits `"null <created_at>"`, and line 1489 then sets `release_blocker_baseline_at` to that unrelated comment's timestamp.
  WHY: Any trusted comment posted after the real marker moves the cycle_stale clock (`max(rb_marker_t, rb_commit_t)`) forward. That can silently suppress `cycle_stale` reports on `base_not_ancestor` and other pre-guard-4 ticks. The bug predates the last run, but the last run made it reachable.

  WHY: Documentation drift only. It misleads API-cost auditing (§14) and debugging of the `lookup=baseline_marker` line.
